title: CTScanClear
question: How does a CT scanner work?
hook: A CT scanner spins an X-ray tube around you three times a second, takes about a thousand shadows each turn, and a computer turns them into slices of your body. Take one apart in 3D, then rebuild a slice yourself with real maths.

explainer.title: A spinning ring of X-rays
explainer.text: Inside the doughnut-shaped gantry, a heavy disc carries an X-ray tube and a curved detector with 64 or more rows of sensors. Slip rings let it spin continuously, once every 0.25 to 0.5 seconds, while the table slides you through.

explainer.title: Hundreds of shadows, one slice
explainer.text: Each detector measures how much X-ray got through along one line. One snapshot is a projection: a 1D shadow of the slice. About 1,000 projections per turn, stacked by angle, make a sinogram. In a helical scan the table moves as the tube spins, so the beam traces a spiral.

explainer.title: Rebuilding the picture
explainer.text: Smear every shadow back across the image and add them up: back-projection. On its own it gives a blurry, streaky slice. Sharpen each shadow first with a ramp (Ram-Lak) filter and the true slice appears. The maths dates from Johann Radon in 1917.

explainer.title: Every pixel is a number
explainer.text: CT measures attenuation and reports it in Hounsfield units: water is 0, air is −1000, fat about −100, bone +400 to over +1000. A window of level and width decides which numbers become grey, so the same scan can show brain, lung or bone.

explainer.title: Dose and speed
explainer.text: A head CT gives about 2 mSv, a chest CT about 7 and an abdomen and pelvis CT about 8 to 10, against about 2.4 mSv a year from nature and 0.02 to 0.1 for a chest X-ray. Lower dose means more noise, so scanners modulate the tube current and use iterative reconstruction. A whole-body trauma scan takes seconds.

explainer.title: Modern tricks
explainer.text: Dual-energy CT uses two X-ray energies to tell materials apart, like uric acid and calcium kidney stones. Cardiac CT times the scan to the ECG. Photon-counting CT, first cleared in 2021, counts every X-ray and measures its energy.

concepts.def: The doughnut-shaped part of a CT scanner that holds the spinning X-ray tube and detector.
The shadow profile of a slice from one angle: how much X-ray each detector received.
All the projections of a slice stacked by angle; each point in the body traces a sine-shaped line in it.
Table travel per rotation divided by the beam width. At pitch 1 the spiral's turns just touch.
Rebuilding a slice by sharpening each projection with a ramp filter and smearing it back across the image.
CT's scale of attenuation: HU = 1000 × (μ − μwater) ÷ μwater, so water is 0 and air is −1000.
The range of Hounsfield units a viewer maps from black to white.
A unit of radiation dose. The world average from natural sources is about 2.4 mSv a year.
Scanning at two X-ray energies to tell materials apart by how their attenuation changes with energy.
